rv.q: Tom Stoppard’s shiveringly sensual journey through the terrible 20th century is a masterpiece.
Tom Stoppard's new masterwork is an early contender for play of the year.

Leopoldstadt is not necessarily better than his previous work but it is different. It is the moment he stopped playing, looked us squarely in the face and said: “As a person, as a playwright, this is what I mean.”
People have sometimes accused him of being too clever by half, lacking the power to move us beyond words; here is irrefutable evidence to the contrary.
